problem: Could any coherent physical framework allow effective faster-than-light travel through spacetime? Investigate the possibility without assuming that a warp-drive mechanism works. Do not constrain the investigation to technologies, materials, energy sources, or engineering methods available today. You may propose extensions, reinterpretations, or replacements of established physical theories, provided each proposal states its mathematical assumptions, internal consistency requirements, compatibility with existing observations, and potentially falsifiable consequences. Analyze the distinction between local motion faster than light and effective superluminal travel through spacetime geometry. Consider causality, horizons, energy conditions, quantum field effects, stability, backreaction, conservation laws, controllability, and the status of exotic stress-energy; do not assume any speculative mechanism works. Compare general-relativistic metric-engineering approaches with at least one fundamentally different conceptual framework. Identify concrete proof obligations, order-of-magnitude constraints where justified, decisive theoretical calculations or observations, and failure criteria. Separate established results, contested literature, hypotheses, and engineering conjectures. Produce a staged research program and a conditional conceptual design, not an unsupported claim of a working drive.

output.claim: Conditional on adopting the explicitly prescribed Lorentzian metric below and its usual light-cone interpretation, a signal can beat the light-travel time between exterior stations in the corresponding unmodified Minkowski spacetime while its carrier remains locally timelike and the modified spacetime has no closed causal curves. This is a kinematic existence result, not evidence that a physical source can create the geometry: the Einstein source required by this particular metric violates the weak energy condition.
output.method: Test the hypothesis that effective superluminal travel necessarily entails either locally superluminal motion or a causal loop. Construct a smooth, finite-duration geometry; compare an operational signal transit time with a specified Minkowski reference; independently inspect the local tangent norm and a global time function. Then use the Einstein constraint to audit the required source and axial characteristics to test onboard controllability. Contrast this geometric construction with a preferred-time, wider-cone field theory. The discriminating outcomes are a shorter exterior-clock transit together with a timelike carrier and a temporal function, versus failure of one of those conditions. All results below are analytical model deductions; no computation, external literature inspection, or physical realization is claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define a finite-duration geometry and the scope of the comparison
reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (-,+,+,+), coordinates (t,x,y,z), and c equal to the local photon speed. Let x_s(t) be smooth and nondecreasing, equal to 0 for t≤0 and L for t≥T, with L>cT. Write v(t)=dx_s/dt and r²=(x-x_s(t))²+y²+z². Choose a smooth radial function 0≤f(r)≤1, equal to 1 near r=0 and 0 for r≥R. Prescribe ds²=-c²dt²+[dx-v(t)f(r)dt]²+dy²+dz². Its determinant is -c², so it remains a nondegenerate Lorentzian metric even when v>c. It is exactly Minkowski before and after the pulse and outside the moving radius-R region. This is a prescribed geometry, not a solution supplied with independently admissible matter. The comparison is between two different geometries with matched exterior clocks, not between a timelike and a null curve in the same metric.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Local motion remains timelike
reasoning_steps.argument: The central carrier follows x=x_s(t), y=z=0. Because f=1 there, substitution gives ds²=-c²dt² and proper time dτ=dt. More generally, define local spatial displacements relative to the unit normal observers by dℓ_x=dx-vf dt, dℓ_y=dy, dℓ_z=dz. The causal condition is dℓ_x²+dℓ_y²+dℓ_z²≤c²dt². The central carrier has zero velocity in this local frame, even if its exterior coordinate velocity v exceeds c. The distinction is therefore geometrical, not a permission for a massive body to cross its local photon cone.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. An exterior-clock protocol establishes the effective shortcut
reasoning_steps.argument: Place stationary stations A at x=-D and B at x=L+D, with D>R. They remain outside the modified region throughout, so their proper times equal t; synchronize them in the common Minkowski past. A sends a light signal at t=-D/c to the central carrier at (t,x)=(0,0). The carrier transports its information to (T,L), then transmits light to B, arriving at t=T+D/c. The first and last light segments lie in the flat pre-pulse and post-pulse regions. The measured elapsed coordinate/synchronized-clock time is T+2D/c, less than the reference Minkowski photon transit (L+2D)/c because L>cT. Thus an operational effective shortcut exists within this prescribed geometry. The geometry must be scheduled independently of the newly transmitted bit; this protocol does not show that A can construct it on demand.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. A global temporal function excludes causal loops in this model
reasoning_steps.argument: The inverse metric satisfies g^{tt}=-1/c² everywhere. Consequently the gradient of t is timelike, and choose the time orientation in which dt is positive on future-directed causal vectors. Along every nontrivial future causal curve, t strictly increases; a closed causal curve is therefore impossible. A timelike gradient also supplies the usual stable-causality criterion. This directly counters the universal claim that every effective shortcut must itself contain a causal loop. It does not license arbitrary moving copies of the shortcut: the familiar reciprocal-signal paradox additionally requires operational access to superluminal channels with suitable relative boosts. Any proposed assembly must have its combined causal structure checked anew.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. The Einstein constraint exposes the source problem
reasoning_steps.argument: For ordinary Einstein gravity with zero cosmological constant, the t-slices have Euclidean spatial metric, unit lapse when using x⁰=ct, and shift β^x=-vf/c. Their extrinsic curvature, up to an irrelevant overall sign convention, is K_ij=-(v/2c)(δ_ix ∂_j f+δ_jx ∂_i f). Hence K²-K_ijK^ij=-(v²/2c²)[(∂_y f)²+(∂_z f)²]. The Hamiltonian constraint gives the normal-observer energy density ε=T_μν n^μ n^ν=c⁴(K²-K_ijK^ij)/(16πG)=-c²v²[(∂_y f)²+(∂_z f)²]/(32πG), in J/m³, where n=(∂_t+vf∂_x)/c. It is negative wherever v≠0 and the transverse wall gradient is nonzero, violating the weak energy condition. This proves a source obstruction for this ansatz, not for every conceivable shortcut. Negative timelike energy density alone is not a derivation of null or averaged-null energy-condition violation.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Quantify the negative-energy scale without confusing it with total mass
reasoning_steps.argument: At a fixed time, angular integration for radial f gives E_normal=∫ε d³x=-(c²v²/12G)∫₀∞r²[f'(r)]²dr. For a wall of thickness Δ≪R, let f=F((r-R)/Δ) across the wall and I=∫[F'(u)]²du. Then E_normal≈-(c²v²/12G)(R²/Δ)I, with relative geometric corrections of order Δ/R for a fixed profile. Its magnitude is approximately 10^47 I (v/c)²(R/100 m)²(1 m/Δ) J. This is an illustrative, profile-dependent negative normal-energy integral, not a fuel requirement, ADM mass, or lower bound on all designs. In particular the asymptotically Euclidean spatial metric here has zero ADM energy; equating that boundary quantity to this volume integral would be erroneous.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. A stationary superluminal segment has a forward characteristic barrier
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose v>c is constant over a sufficiently long cruise segment. On the axis set ξ=x-x_s(t). Forward-directed axial null rays obey dξ/dt=c-v[1-f(|ξ|)]. For a wall profile decreasing toward the front, this vanishes at f=1-c/v. Starting at the center, the outward characteristic approaches this stationary front barrier rather than crossing it during indefinitely stationary cruise. This restricts control signals sent from the cabin to the leading exterior. It is not a proof of a permanent event horizon for the finite pulse: switching the geometry off changes the global causal structure. The prescribed schedule hides precisely the formation and control problem that a working drive would have to solve.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Conservation and quantum consistency are additional, not automatic, successes
reasoning_steps.argument: Defining T_μν=c⁴G_μν/(8πG) ensures ∇_μT^{μν}=0 by the contracted Bianchi identity. This geometric identity does not produce matter fields, an actuator, a Hamiltonian bounded below, or an initial-value construction. A semiclassical proposal instead must solve G_μν=(8πG/c⁴)(T_classical,μν+⟨T_μν⟩_ren) for a specified quantum state and renormalization prescription. Local negative quantum energy is not by itself a source for the required macroscopic tensor. Quantum energy inequalities must be applied with their actual field, state, trajectory and sampling assumptions. Finite-duration characteristic barriers alone establish neither a universal stress divergence nor its absence; renormalized stress, fluctuations and backreaction remain to be calculated.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. A fundamentally different comparison: wider cones with preferred time
reasoning_steps.argument: As a separate toy framework, keep photon/matter Minkowski geometry but introduce a preferred-time scalar with action S=(1/2)∫dt d³x[(∂_tφ)²-s²|∇φ|²-Ω²φ²], where s>c has units m/s, Ω≥0 has units s⁻¹, and the field normalization supplies action units. Its equation is ∂_t²φ-s²∇²φ+Ω²φ=0, dispersion is ω²=s²k²+Ω², and Hamiltonian density is [(∂_tφ)²+s²|∇φ|²+Ω²φ²]/2≥0. Its characteristic signal-front speed is s, unlike the photon speed c. Restricting all interactions to evolution forward in the same preferred t avoids causal loops at this free-field level. This is local superluminality relative to the photon cone, not geometric transport of an ordinary timelike craft. It abandons universal Lorentz symmetry rather than ordinary local light-cone motion. A usable interacting detector/source sector, stability under coupling, radiative corrections and compatibility with observations are unproved; the free scalar is not a travel mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Conditional design and staged decision gates
reasoning_steps.argument: The geometric conceptual design is a prearranged compact corridor carrying a central timelike relay, with exterior clocks and a finite start/stop schedule. Gate 1 is the analytical kinematic test above; it passes for the prescribed metric. Gate 2 is a covariant source model and constraint-satisfying initial data that generate the corridor without already requiring the desired signal to outrun its available control cones; the present construction does not pass this gate. Gate 3 is coupled classical and semiclassical evolution, including perturbation growth, source dynamics, stress fluctuations and backreaction. Gate 4 is an operational formation/control protocol and a full multiple-trip causality audit. Gate 5 is observational confrontation of the source model or preferred-cone alternative. Failure of source admissibility, an ill-posed initial-value problem, destructive backreaction, inaccessible controls, or excluded Lorentz-violating couplings rejects that candidate, not every coherent framework. The next decisive calculation is Gate 2 for a specified source, rather than further optimization of an unconstrained metric.

assumptions: For the kinematic claim, spacetime is assigned the smooth metric in step 1 regardless of whether any admissible physical source can generate it.
Signals and ordinary carriers obey the causal cones of that metric, with the future orientation selected by increasing t.
The exterior stations, prearranged carrier trajectory and information relays are idealized test systems; their backreaction is neglected.
The stress-energy audit additionally assumes ordinary Einstein gravity, zero cosmological constant and the stated asymptotically flat boundary conditions.
The preferred-time scalar is a separate free-field toy theory, not an assumed replacement that has passed observational or interacting-theory tests.
output.evidence_status: Analytical kinematic and Einstein-constraint deductions for an explicit prescribed metric; no execution, independent verification, or physical source construction. The broader existence of a realizable travel framework remains unresolved. Literature priority and empirical viability have not been assessed.
open_obligations: Supply a specific dynamical source action and solve its coupled constraints and evolution, rather than identifying an Einstein tensor with realizable matter. The explicit metric already fails the weak energy condition.
Determine formation, switching and leading-wall control from admissible initial data; distinguish predeployed infrastructure from a self-contained craft.
Calculate applicable null/averaged energy constraints, quantum energy inequalities, renormalized stress and fluctuations for a specified field and state; then solve or bound backreaction.
Establish perturbative and nonlinear stability and audit causal structure after multiple corridors, relative motion and interactions are included.

For the preferred-time alternative, construct an interacting, stable source/detector sector and establish observable limits on preferred-frame effects, extra radiation channels and radiative corrections. Signal transmission alone would not establish material transport.

No observational dataset or original domain literature was available for inspection. Compatibility with existing tests, contested quantum-instability claims, and material novelty require separate source-based review.

output.claim: For the explicitly defined flat-slice warp metric below, the Einstein constraint equation requires negative energy density wherever the shape function has a nonzero transverse gradient. For a spherical compact wall, its negative slice-energy integral obeys an exact lower bound in magnitude, scaling as c^4 β^2 R^2/(12GΔ) for a thin wall. This is a conditional stress-energy requirement, not evidence that suitable matter, controllability, or a working superluminal drive exists.
output.method: Audit one prescribed geometry analytically rather than assume a mechanism. Hypothesis: its required Einstein source violates the weak energy condition even below the nominal superluminal threshold. The discriminating calculation is the Hamiltonian constraint; a nonnegative result would defeat that hypothesis. Independently check dimensions, the zero-velocity and constant-profile limits, and derive a profile-independent wall bound by Cauchy–Schwarz. Separate local causal motion from asymptotic travel comparisons, and compare the geometric construction with a preferred-time, wider-cone field theory. Neither runtime nor external-source retrieval is available, so the results are hand derivations without computational or literature verification. Novelty is not assessed.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the geometry and physical conventions
reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (−,+,+,+), x^0=ct, zero cosmological constant, and Einstein's equation G_ab=8πG T_ab/c^4. Consider ds²=−(dx^0)²+[dx−β f(r)dx^0]²+dy²+dz², where β=v/c is constant, r²=(x−βx^0)²+y²+z², and f is smooth, equals one for r≤R, and vanishes for r≥R+Δ, with R,Δ>0. This is a prescribed metric, not a derived matter solution. Its lapse is one, spatial metric is Euclidean, and ADM shift is B^i=(−βf,0,0). The unit future normal is n^a=(1,βf,0,0). Define ε=T_ab n^a n^b, in J/m³.

reasoning_steps.title: Evaluate the constraint source
reasoning_steps.argument: With K_ij=−(1/2)L_n h_ij, the time-independent spatial metric gives K_ij=(∂_i B_j+∂_j B_i)/2. Thus K_xx=−β f_x, K_xy=−β f_y/2, K_xz=−β f_z/2, and the other independent components vanish. Consequently K²=β²f_x² and K_ij K^ij=β²f_x²+(β²/2)(f_y²+f_z²). The Hamiltonian constraint, ³R+K²−K_ij K^ij=16πG ε/c^4, with ³R=0, yields ε=−c^4β²(f_y²+f_z²)/(32πG). The result is unchanged by reversing the convention for K.

reasoning_steps.title: Identify precisely which energy conditions fail
reasoning_steps.argument: For β≠0, ε<0 wherever the transverse gradient is nonzero. Since n is a physically admissible timelike observer, the weak energy condition fails there; the dominant energy condition therefore fails as well. For spherical f, f_y²+f_z²=(f′)²sin²θ, with θ measured from the x axis, so every nontrivial smooth wall has an open negative-density region. This calculation alone does not prove null-energy-condition violation: that requires contractions T_ab k^a k^b including pressures and momentum flux. It also says nothing by itself about averaged conditions or quantum energy inequalities.

reasoning_steps.title: Integrate the requirement without misidentifying total energy
reasoning_steps.argument: The proper spatial volume is d³x. Angular integration gives E_n≡∫ε d³x=−[c^4β²/(12G)]∫_R^(R+Δ)r²(f′)²dr, because ∫sin²θ dΩ=8π/3. This is a specified Eulerian slice integral, not a conserved total mass or an engineering fuel requirement. Indeed the standard ADM energy surface integral vanishes because the spatial metric is exactly Euclidean; the compactly supported extrinsic curvature also gives zero ADM momentum. Thus negative E_n must not be equated with negative ADM mass. The positive-energy theorem cannot be invoked under its usual dominant-energy premise, which this source violates.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive a profile-independent bound
reasoning_steps.argument: Since ∫_R^(R+Δ)f′dr=−1, Cauchy–Schwarz gives 1≤[∫r²(f′)²dr][∫r^(−2)dr]. The second factor is Δ/[R(R+Δ)], hence |E_n|≥[c^4β²/(12G)]R(R+Δ)/Δ. No monotonicity assumption is needed. Equality requires f′ proportional to r^(−2) throughout the wall, incompatible with smooth matching to both constant regions, but the lower bound remains valid. At Δ≪R the leading scaling is R²/Δ. The bound is not claimed for R=0, nonspherical profiles, nonflat spatial slices, or another lapse/shift ansatz.

reasoning_steps.title: Check limiting cases, units, and scale
reasoning_steps.argument: Both the local density and E_n vanish at β=0 or for constant f, consistent with absence of this wall curvature source. Since c^4/G has units J/m, the energy formula has units J. Using c≈3.00×10^8 m/s and G≈6.67×10^−11 m³ kg^−1 s^−2 gives c^4/G≈1.21×10^44 J/m. For R=100 m, Δ=1 m and β=2, the bound is approximately |E_n|≥4.1×10^47 J, with mass-equivalent magnitude |E_n|/c²≈4.5×10^30 kg. These are approximate arithmetic estimates of a model-specific slice integral, not available negative energy or a universal FTL cost.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate local motion from an effective travel claim
reasoning_steps.argument: At the center, x=βx^0 and f=1, so ds²=−(dx^0)²: the central trajectory is timelike even when β>1. Every local freely falling observer still measures the metric light cone with invariant speed c. β>1 instead describes displacement relative to the asymptotically Minkowski coordinates. An operational effective-superluminal claim additionally needs a complete preparation and arrival spacetime, specified distant clocks, and comparison with a reference light signal. The eternal constant-speed metric alone does not supply that experiment.

reasoning_steps.title: Expose an axial control obstruction in the stationary model
reasoning_steps.argument: For forward axial null propagation, put ξ=x−βx^0 and y=z=0. The null equation becomes dξ/dx^0=1−β[1−f(|ξ|)]. If β>1 and f decreases monotonically across the front wall, this derivative changes from +1 inside to 1−β<0 outside and vanishes at f=1−1/β. Smoothness gives a locally Lipschitz autonomous equation: a ray starting inside cannot cross that equilibrium in finite x^0. This establishes an axial outward-signal obstruction for the eternal stationary model, not a complete global horizon classification or a theorem excluding every external control scheme. A finite-duration construction must recompute the causal structure rather than inherit an assumed horizon.

reasoning_steps.title: Explain why a conserved geometric source is not a material mechanism
reasoning_steps.argument: Defining T_ab=c^4G_ab/(8πG) automatically gives ∇^aT_ab=0 by the contracted Bianchi identity. This satisfies a necessary conservation identity but does not establish a matter action, well-posed matter evolution, a realizable quantum state, or a way to prepare the source. No horizon divergence, quantum instability, or quantum-inequality exclusion has been established here. Those require a specified field theory, state and boundary conditions, renormalized stress tensor, and backreaction analysis. Negative expectation values allowed in some quantum settings cannot simply be substituted for the required full tensor.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct a fundamentally different conditional causal framework
reasoning_steps.argument: As a contrasting toy model, assume a physical preferred global time T in flat spacetime, ordinary light speed c, and a real field χ with Lagrangian density L=(1/2)[(∂_Tχ)²−c_s²|∇χ|²−ω_0²χ²], where c_s>c and ω_0²≥0. Its equation is ∂_T²χ−c_s²∇²χ+ω_0²χ=0, its Hamiltonian density is nonnegative, and its dispersion is ω²=c_s²k²+ω_0². For ω_0=0 its disturbances propagate at c_s. Assuming every physical future-directed channel increases this same single-valued T, a closed causal route is impossible because its accumulated increase in T cannot be zero. This explicitly replaces boost symmetry rather than deriving a superluminal channel within Lorentz-invariant matter.

reasoning_steps.title: Limit the alternative and specify observations that distinguish it
reasoning_steps.argument: The free preferred-time model demonstrates limited mathematical consistency, not compatibility with observed matter or transport of a payload. Its conserved energy follows from T-translation symmetry; interactions and a dynamical gravity sector remain unspecified. Observable coupling would predict signal propagation outside the ordinary light cone and a preferred-frame dependence relative to material clocks. Absence of those effects at the coupling strength needed for control would exclude that parameter choice. A completely decoupled sector evades such tests but supplies no usable travel mechanism. No observational dataset or numerical bound has been inspected, so empirical compatibility remains unresolved. By contrast, the audited metric preserves local metric light cones but requires exotic Einstein stress-energy.

reasoning_steps.title: Turn the stress audit into a gated research program
reasoning_steps.argument: Stage 1: independently derive the full Einstein tensor and its orthonormal components, then evaluate pointwise and averaged null contractions; disagreement with the constraint above requires correction before further interpretation. Stage 2: propose an explicit source action and initial data, solve its constraints, and test hyperbolicity and perturbation stability; failure to reproduce the required tensor or a loss of well-posedness rejects that source candidate. Stage 3: for any quantum source, calculate its renormalized stress and fluctuations and solve semiclassical backreaction in the domain where that approximation is justified. Stage 4: replace eternal motion with formation, finite transit and shutdown, demonstrating causal control, acceptable tidal exposure and an operational arrival advantage. The conditional conceptual design is therefore an externally prepared, finite-duration geometric corridor with timelike payload motion, contingent on passing every earlier gate—not an onboard working drive. In parallel, the preferred-time branch must supply stable interacting matter and gravity and then confront preferred-frame and signal-speed observations. Failure of either branch does not establish a no-go theorem for all possible frameworks.

output.response:
The conditional stress-energy claim is supported by the supplied derivation. The Hamiltonian constraint, angular integral, Cauchy–Schwarz bound, dimensions, and quoted numerical scale check out. Crucially, the negative slice integral is not ADM mass or a demonstrated fuel requirement.

An additional analytic check advances the null-energy question. Define q=f_y²+f_z², e_x^a=(0,1,0,0), and k_±=n±e_x. For the stated constant-β metric, the projected Ricci identities give R_nn+R_xx=−β²q and R_nx=(β/2)(f_yy+f_zz). Consequently,
T_ab k_±^a k_±^b = [c⁴/(8πG)][−β²q ± β(f_yy+f_zz)].
Their sum is −c⁴β²q/(4πG), so wherever q>0 at least one null direction violates the pointwise NEC. This is a hand-derived local result, not an averaged-energy theorem or independent formal verification. It also does not supply the remaining source components or a realizable matter model.

The original geometry has another useful causal limitation: g^{00}=−1 makes x⁰ a global time function on its stated coordinate domain, excluding closed metric-causal curves within that spacetime. This does not establish causal consistency of arbitrary combined or modified transport arrangements.

The overall objective remains partial. The preferred-time field is a mathematically coherent free-field comparison, not an observationally validated interacting theory or payload mechanism. reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (−,+,+,+), c=ℏ=1, κ=8πG, and S=∫√−g[R/(2κ)+P(X,φ)]d⁴x, with X=−g^{μν}∂_μφ∂_νφ/2. P is smooth with finite derivatives on the background. Taking φ to have energy units gives X and P units energy⁴, P_X dimensionless and P_XX units energy⁻⁴. The necessary local gate is a physical scalar mode with a nondegenerate Lorentzian principal symbol, a common spacelike initial surface with gravity, and positive high-frequency kinetic and gradient energies relative to the ordinary positive-energy gravitational sector. Passing this gate would not establish nonlinear stability or quantum consistency.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Re-establish the target's null-energy requirement
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the metric explicitly reproduced in the supplied cycle-2 extract: ds²=−dt²+(dx−b dt)²+dy²+dz², b=v(t)f. Define n=∂t+b∂x and e_x=∂x, an orthonormal timelike–spacelike pair. Writing b_i=∂_i b and Q=b_y²+b_z², direct curvature evaluation gives R(n,n)=−n(b_x)−b_x²−Q/2 and R(e_x,e_x)=n(b_x)+b_x²−Q/2. Thus R(n,n)+R(e_x,e_x)=−Q, including a time-dependent pulse; time derivatives cancel rather than being neglected. Einstein's equation implies T(n,n)+T(e_x,e_x)=−Q/κ. For k_±=n±e_x, T(k_+,k_+)+T(k_−,k_−)=−2Q/κ. At least one null contraction is strictly negative wherever the transverse wall gradient is nonzero. This conclusion does not follow merely from negative normal energy; the null contraction is an additional calculation.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Distinguish the geometry from local superluminal motion
reasoning_steps.argument: In that metric, a trajectory with dx=b dt and dy=dz=0 has ds²=−dt², and axial light rays obey dx/dt=b±1. Coordinate speeds exceeding one therefore need not mean motion outside the local metric light cone. Also g^{tt}=−1, so increasing t is a temporal orientation for this prescribed geometry. Neither observation supplies matter capable of producing it, establishes preparation or leading-wall control, or settles causality after combining configurations. The present calculation tests the source, not a working transport mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Derive null stress, equations and conservation
reasoning_steps.argument: Let u_μ=∂_μφ, A=P_X and B=P_XX. Variation gives T_μν=A u_μu_ν+P g_μν and E≡∇_μ(A∇^μφ)+P_φ=0. Consequently T_μνk^μk^ν=A(k·u)² for every metric-null k. Strict negative null stress requires A<0 and a nonzero contraction; the potential-like P term cannot change this sign. The identity ∇_μT^{μν}=E∇^νφ ensures stress conservation on solutions. Expanding E shows its second-derivative coefficient is Z^{μν}=A g^{μν}−B u^μu^ν; the remaining terms include P_φ−2X P_Xφ and are lower derivative.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Obtain the complete fixed-metric quadratic scalar action
reasoning_steps.argument: For φ=φ̄+π on a background solution, δX=−u·∇π−(∇π)²/2. The quadratic Lagrangian is L₂=−A(∇π)²/2+B(u·∇π)²/2−P_Xφ π u·∇π+P_φφ π²/2. Integrating the mixed term by parts yields L₂=−Z^{μν}∇_μπ∇_νπ/2+Uπ²/2, where U=P_φφ+∇_μ(P_Xφ u^μ). U has units energy². This is the fixed-background second variation; its frozen-coefficient principal part is the necessary short-wavelength test. Background variation and U affect long wavelengths but cannot reverse the leading derivative signs in a controlled high-frequency regime.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. A general-slicing Hamiltonian exposes the obstruction
reasoning_steps.argument: At a point choose a metric-orthonormal frame adapted to an arbitrary timelike normal and set q=∂tφ̄, s_i=∂iφ̄, so u^μ=(−q,s_i). Define K=A+Bq². Then L₂=Kπ̇²/2−Bqπ̇(s·∇π)−[A|∇π|²−B(s·∇π)²]/2+Uπ²/2. For K≠0, p=Kπ̇−Bq(s·∇π) and H₂=[p+Bq(s·∇π)]²/(2K)+[A|∇π|²−B(s·∇π)²]/2−Uπ²/2. If A<0 and K>0, take a wavevector perpendicular to s. The cross term vanishes and ω²=(A|k|²−U)/K, negative at sufficiently large |k|. Its growth rate approaches |k|√(−A/K). If K<0, the momentum-square term is negative: a ghost relative to ordinary matter and gravity. K=0 makes that slicing characteristic for the scalar. This argument holds for every metric-timelike normal and prevents a change of common slicing from restoring positive high-frequency energy.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Timelike-gradient classification
reasoning_steps.argument: For X>0 use the scalar rest frame u_μ=(√(2X),0,0,0) and define F=A+2XB. Then Z=diag(−F,A,A,A), L₂=Fπ̇²/2−A|∇π|²/2+Uπ²/2 and H₂=p²/(2F)+A|∇π|²/2−Uπ²/2. The frozen dispersion is ω²=(A/F)|k|²−U/F. Positive high-frequency energy requires F>0 and A>0, giving sound speed squared c_s²=A/F. If A<0,F>0 there is a gradient instability and the symbol is definite rather than Lorentzian. If A<0,F<0 the symbol is Lorentzian but the mode has negative kinetic energy. More generally, for nonzero A,F, timelike-gradient hyperbolicity requires AF>0; hyperbolicity alone does not select the healthy overall sign.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Spacelike-gradient classification
reasoning_steps.argument: For X<0 use u_μ=(0,√(−2X),0,0). Now Z=diag(−A,F,A,A), H₂=p²/(2A)+F(∂xπ)²/2+A[(∂yπ)²+(∂zπ)²]/2−Uπ²/2 and ω²=|k_⊥|²+(F/A)k_x²−U/A. Positive high-frequency energy again requires A>0,F>0. For A<0 the kinetic term is a ghost, regardless of B; varying B changes only the longitudinal spatial coefficient. With AF<0 the symbol has two eigenvalues of each sign and is not an ordinary Lorentzian wave operator. With A<0,F<0 it is Lorentzian but has the wrong energy sign. Thus choosing a spacelike background gradient does not evade the obstruction.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Null and zero-gradient backgrounds
reasoning_steps.argument: For a nonzero null gradient choose u_μ=(q,q,0,0), X=0. The principal-symbol determinant is det Z=−A⁴ in a metric-orthonormal frame, so A≠0 gives a Lorentzian symbol even for finite nonzero B. Nevertheless the general Hamiltonian test applies: if A<0, K=A+Bq² is either negative, zero, or positive with unstable transverse modes. A Lorentzian symbol therefore does not rescue negative null stress. For A>0 a boost can make |q| small enough that both kinetic and spatial-gradient coefficients are positive locally; its null stress is then nonnegative. If u=0, Z=A g and all null stresses vanish; A<0 is an ordinary wrong-sign scalar, while A=0 has no quadratic derivative term.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Degenerate boundaries for non-null gradients
reasoning_steps.argument: The determinant identity is det Z=−A³F. For X>0, A=0,F≠0 leaves only a time-derivative quadratic term: F>0 is not itself a ghost, but there is no spatial restoring term and no nondegenerate wave cone. F=0,A≠0 removes the rest-frame time kinetic term, leaving a spatial constraint rather than a scalar wave equation. For X<0, A=0,F≠0 leaves only a longitudinal spatial derivative and no time kinetic term; F=0,A≠0 leaves a rank-three operator describing transverse propagation without a longitudinal principal derivative. If A=F=0 at nonzero X, then B=0 and the derivative quadratic form vanishes entirely. These are rank deficiencies, not automatically proofs of inconsistency of every possible constrained formulation. A=0, however, gives zero—not strictly negative—null stress; F=0 with A<0 does not provide a regular positive-energy scalar wave.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Null degeneracy, constrained exceptions and crossing boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: For nonzero null u and A=0, Z=−B u^μu^ν has rank one when B≠0 and rank zero when B=0. It is not a nondegenerate hyperbolic scalar operator and its null stress vanishes. A concrete different boundary is P=−μ²√(2X)−V(φ) on X>0: A=−μ²/√(2X)<0 but F=0. It can violate the null energy condition, yet its scalar equation has a spatial-constraint principal part in the gradient rest frame, not a propagating hyperbolic scalar. Whether a coupled constrained model of this kind is predictive and stable needs a separate elliptic–hyperbolic analysis; it is not ruled out as incoherent here. Higher-derivative terms can also change degenerate dispersion, but change the specified action. Smooth passage through A=0 cannot avoid the obstruction inside any open region where strict negative null stress requires A<0.

reasoning_steps.argument: In a regular minimally coupled Einstein–P system, the linearized Einstein equations contain second derivatives of the metric, but δT contains at most first derivatives of π. The scalar equation contains second derivatives of π with coefficient Z and at most first derivatives of metric perturbations through connection variations and coefficient derivatives. Thus the leading second-order principal blocks in harmonic gauge are the Einstein wave block and Z. In a short-wavelength regime above background, mass and mixing scales, gravitational constraints do not reverse the scalar principal energy sign; choosing unitary gauge merely relocates the physical scalar perturbation into the metric variables. investigator_output.method: Test the hypothesis that effective superluminal travel necessarily entails either locally superluminal motion or a causal loop. Construct a smooth, finite-duration geometry; compare an operational signal transit time with a specified Minkowski reference; independently inspect the local tangent norm and a global time function. Then use the Einstein constraint to audit the required source and axial characteristics to test onboard controllability. Contrast this geometric construction with a preferred-time, wider-cone field theory. The discriminating outcomes are a shorter exterior-clock transit together with a timelike carrier and a temporal function, versus failure of one of those conditions. All results below are analytical model deductions; no computation, external literature inspection, or physical realization is claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define a finite-duration geometry and the scope of the comparison
reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (-,+,+,+), coordinates (t,x,y,z), and c equal to the local photon speed. Let x_s(t) be smooth and nondecreasing, equal to 0 for t≤0 and L for t≥T, with L>cT. Write v(t)=dx_s/dt and r²=(x-x_s(t))²+y²+z². Choose a smooth radial function 0≤f(r)≤1, equal to 1 near r=0 and 0 for r≥R. Prescribe ds²=-c²dt²+[dx-v(t)f(r)dt]²+dy²+dz². Its determinant is -c², so it remains a nondegenerate Lorentzian metric even when v>c. It is exactly Minkowski before and after the pulse and outside the moving radius-R region. This is a prescribed geometry, not a solution supplied with independently admissible matter. The comparison is between two different geometries with matched exterior clocks, not between a timelike and a null curve in the same metric.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Local motion remains timelike
reasoning_steps.argument: The central carrier follows x=x_s(t), y=z=0. Because f=1 there, substitution gives ds²=-c²dt² and proper time dτ=dt. More generally, define local spatial displacements relative to the unit normal observers by dℓ_x=dx-vf dt, dℓ_y=dy, dℓ_z=dz. The causal condition is dℓ_x²+dℓ_y²+dℓ_z²≤c²dt². The central carrier has zero velocity in this local frame, even if its exterior coordinate velocity v exceeds c. The distinction is therefore geometrical, not a permission for a massive body to cross its local photon cone.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. An exterior-clock protocol establishes the effective shortcut
reasoning_steps.argument: Place stationary stations A at x=-D and B at x=L+D, with D>R. They remain outside the modified region throughout, so their proper times equal t; synchronize them in the common Minkowski past. A sends a light signal at t=-D/c to the central carrier at (t,x)=(0,0). The carrier transports its information to (T,L), then transmits light to B, arriving at t=T+D/c. The first and last light segments lie in the flat pre-pulse and post-pulse regions. The measured elapsed coordinate/synchronized-clock time is T+2D/c, less than the reference Minkowski photon transit (L+2D)/c because L>cT. Thus an operational effective shortcut exists within this prescribed geometry. The geometry must be scheduled independently of the newly transmitted bit; this protocol does not show that A can construct it on demand.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. A global temporal function excludes causal loops in this model
reasoning_steps.argument: The inverse metric satisfies g^{tt}=-1/c² everywhere. Consequently the gradient of t is timelike, and choose the time orientation in which dt is positive on future-directed causal vectors. Along every nontrivial future causal curve, t strictly increases; a closed causal curve is therefore impossible. A timelike gradient also supplies the usual stable-causality criterion. This directly counters the universal claim that every effective shortcut must itself contain a causal loop. It does not license arbitrary moving copies of the shortcut: the familiar reciprocal-signal paradox additionally requires operational access to superluminal channels with suitable relative boosts. Any proposed assembly must have its combined causal structure checked anew.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. The Einstein constraint exposes the source problem
reasoning_steps.argument: For ordinary Einstein gravity with zero cosmological constant, the t-slices have Euclidean spatial metric, unit lapse when using x⁰=ct, and shift β^x=-vf/c. reasoning_steps.title: 6. Quantify the negative-energy scale without confusing it with total mass

reasoning_steps.title: Define the geometry and physical conventions
reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (−,+,+,+), x^0=ct, zero cosmological constant, and Einstein's equation G_ab=8πG T_ab/c^4. Consider ds²=−(dx^0)²+[dx−β f(r)dx^0]²+dy²+dz², where β=v/c is constant, r²=(x−βx^0)²+y²+z², and f is smooth, equals one for r≤R, and vanishes for r≥R+Δ, with R,Δ>0. This is a prescribed metric, not a derived matter solution. Its lapse is one, spatial metric is Euclidean, and ADM shift is B^i=(−βf,0,0). The unit future normal is n^a=(1,βf,0,0). Define ε=T_ab n^a n^b, in J/m³.

reasoning_steps.title: Evaluate the constraint source
reasoning_steps.argument: With K_ij=−(1/2)L_n h_ij, the time-independent spatial metric gives K_ij=(∂_i B_j+∂_j B_i)/2. Thus K_xx=−β f_x, K_xy=−β f_y/2, K_xz=−β f_z/2, and the other independent components vanish. Consequently K²=β²f_x² and K_ij K^ij=β²f_x²+(β²/2)(f_y²+f_z²). The Hamiltonian constraint, ³R+K²−K_ij K^ij=16πG ε/c^4, with ³R=0, yields ε=−c^4β²(f_y²+f_z²)/(32πG). The result is unchanged by reversing the convention for K.

reasoning_steps.title: Identify precisely which energy conditions fail
reasoning_steps.argument: For β≠0, ε<0 wherever the transverse gradient is nonzero. Since n is a physically admissible timelike observer, the weak energy condition fails there; the dominant energy condition therefore fails as well. For spherical f, f_y²+f_z²=(f′)²sin²θ, with θ measured from the x axis, so every nontrivial smooth wall has an open negative-density region. This calculation alone does not prove null-energy-condition violation: that requires contractions T_ab k^a k^b including pressures and momentum flux. It also says nothing by itself about averaged conditions or quantum energy inequalities.

reasoning_steps.title: Integrate the requirement without misidentifying total energy
reasoning_steps.argument: The proper spatial volume is d³x. Angular integration gives E_n≡∫ε d³x=−[c^4β²/(12G)]∫_R^(R+Δ)r²(f′)²dr, because ∫sin²θ dΩ=8π/3. This is a specified Eulerian slice integral, not a conserved total mass or an engineering fuel requirement. Indeed the standard ADM energy surface integral vanishes because the spatial metric is exactly Euclidean; the compactly supported extrinsic curvature also gives zero ADM momentum. Thus negative E_n must not be equated with negative ADM mass. The positive-energy theorem cannot be invoked under its usual dominant-energy premise, which this source violates.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive a profile-independent bound
reasoning_steps.argument: Since ∫_R^(R+Δ)f′dr=−1, Cauchy–Schwarz gives 1≤[∫r²(f′)²dr][∫r^(−2)dr]. The second factor is Δ/[R(R+Δ)], hence |E_n|≥[c^4β²/(12G)]R(R+Δ)/Δ. No monotonicity assumption is needed. Equality requires f′ proportional to r^(−2) throughout the wall, incompatible with smooth matching to both constant regions, but the lower bound remains valid. argument_steps.title: Define the geometry and physical conventions
argument_steps.argument: Use signature (−,+,+,+), x^0=ct, zero cosmological constant, and Einstein's equation G_ab=8πG T_ab/c^4. Consider ds²=−(dx^0)²+[dx−β f(r)dx^0]²+dy²+dz², where β=v/c is constant, r²=(x−βx^0)²+y²+z², and f is smooth, equals one for r≤R, and vanishes for r≥R+Δ, with R,Δ>0. This is a prescribed metric, not a derived matter solution. Its lapse is one, spatial metric is Euclidean, and ADM shift is B^i=(−βf,0,0). The unit future normal is n^a=(1,βf,0,0). Define ε=T_ab n^a n^b, in J/m³.

review.rationale: Accepted as an explicit conditional premise, not a physical existence result. Expanding the metric gives the stated shift and unit normal; contracting n with the metric gives −1. The listed gravity and profile assumptions match the conditional claim.

argument_steps.title: Evaluate the constraint source
argument_steps.argument: With K_ij=−(1/2)L_n h_ij, the time-independent spatial metric gives K_ij=(∂_i B_j+∂_j B_i)/2. Thus K_xx=−β f_x, K_xy=−β f_y/2, K_xz=−β f_z/2, and the other independent components vanish. Consequently K²=β²f_x² and K_ij K^ij=β²f_x²+(β²/2)(f_y²+f_z²). The Hamiltonian constraint, ³R+K²−K_ij K^ij=16πG ε/c^4, with ³R=0, yields ε=−c^4β²(f_y²+f_z²)/(32πG). The result is unchanged by reversing the convention for K.

review.rationale: For the stated extrinsic-curvature convention, the flat spatial metric gives the displayed K components. Their squared contraction differs from K² by β²(f_y²+f_z²)/2, producing exactly the stated density through the Hamiltonian constraint.

argument_steps.title: Identify precisely which energy conditions fail
argument_steps.argument: For β≠0, ε<0 wherever the transverse gradient is nonzero. Since n is a physically admissible timelike observer, the weak energy condition fails there; the dominant energy condition therefore fails as well. For spherical f, f_y²+f_z²=(f′)²sin²θ, with θ measured from the x axis, so every nontrivial smooth wall has an open negative-density region. This calculation alone does not prove null-energy-condition violation: that requires contractions T_ab k^a k^b including pressures and momentum flux. It also says nothing by itself about averaged conditions or quantum energy inequalities.

review.rationale: A negative contraction with the admissible timelike normal violates WEC and hence DEC. A nonconstant smooth spherical wall has nonzero transverse derivative on an open region. The warning that this density calculation alone does not establish NEC or averaged conditions is logically correct; the additional contractions in this review advance only the pointwise NEC question.

argument_steps.title: Integrate the requirement without misidentifying total energy
argument_steps.argument: The proper spatial volume is d³x. Angular integration gives E_n≡∫ε d³x=−[c^4β²/(12G)]∫_R^(R+Δ)r²(f′)²dr, because ∫sin²θ dΩ=8π/3. This is a specified Eulerian slice integral, not a conserved total mass or an engineering fuel requirement. Indeed the standard ADM energy surface integral vanishes because the spatial metric is exactly Euclidean; the compactly supported extrinsic curvature also gives zero ADM momentum. Thus negative E_n must not be equated with negative ADM mass. The positive-energy theorem cannot be invoked under its usual dominant-energy premise, which this source violates.

review.rationale: The slice volume is Euclidean and the angular factor is 8π/3, giving the stated coefficient. Euclidean spatial asymptotics give zero ADM energy, while compactly supported K gives zero ADM momentum. These surface charges are correctly distinguished from the normal-density volume integral.

argument_steps.title: Derive a profile-independent bound
argument_steps.argument: Since ∫_R^(R+Δ)f′dr=−1, Cauchy–Schwarz gives 1≤[∫r²(f′)²dr][∫r^(−2)dr]. The second factor is Δ/[R(R+Δ)], hence |E_n|≥[c^4β²/(12G)]R(R+Δ)/Δ. No monotonicity assumption is needed. Equality requires f′ proportional to r^(−2) throughout the wall, incompatible with smooth matching to both constant regions, but the lower bound remains valid. At Δ≪R the leading scaling is R²/Δ. The bound is not claimed for R=0, nonspherical profiles, nonflat spatial slices, or another lapse/shift ansatz.

review.rationale: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to rf′ and 1/r, using the endpoint change −1. The reciprocal integral is Δ/[R(R+Δ)], giving the exact bound. Its equality profile cannot smoothly match both constant regions; monotonicity is unnecessary.

argument_steps.title: Check limiting cases, units, and scale
argument_steps.argument: Both the local density and E_n vanish at β=0 or for constant f, consistent with absence of this wall curvature source. Since c^4/G has units J/m, the energy formula has units J. Using c≈3.00×10^8 m/s and G≈6.67×10^−11 m³ kg^−1 s^−2 gives c^4/G≈1.21×10^44 J/m. For R=100 m, Δ=1 m and β=2, the bound is approximately |E_n|≥4.1×10^47 J, with mass-equivalent magnitude |E_n|/c²≈4.5×10^30 kg. These are approximate arithmetic estimates of a model-specific slice integral, not available negative energy or a universal FTL cost.

review.rationale: The vanishing limits and dimensions are correct. Substitution gives approximately 4.1×10^47 J and 4.5×10^30 kg for the stated parameters. These are bounded arithmetic estimates of the defined slice integral, not measurements or universal propulsion costs.

argument_steps.argument: At the center, x=βx^0 and f=1, so ds²=−(dx^0)²: the central trajectory is timelike even when β>1. argument_steps.title: Expose an axial control obstruction in the stationary model
argument_steps.argument: For forward axial null propagation, put ξ=x−βx^0 and y=z=0. The null equation becomes dξ/dx^0=1−β[1−f(|ξ|)]. If β>1 and f decreases monotonically across the front wall, this derivative changes from +1 inside to 1−β<0 outside and vanishes at f=1−1/β. Smoothness gives a locally Lipschitz autonomous equation: a ray starting inside cannot cross that equilibrium in finite x^0. This establishes an axial outward-signal obstruction for the eternal stationary model, not a complete global horizon classification or a theorem excluding every external control scheme. A finite-duration construction must recompute the causal structure rather than inherit an assumed horizon.

review.rationale: The forward axial null branch gives the displayed autonomous equation. For β>1 its right-hand side changes sign across a monotone front wall. Smoothness implies local uniqueness, preventing a solution from crossing the stationary equilibrium in finite coordinate time. The claim is appropriately restricted to axial outward signaling in the eternal geometry.

review.rationale: The contracted Bianchi identity guarantees covariant conservation of the geometrically defined source, but does not entail a matter action or realizable state. argument_steps.title: Construct a fundamentally different conditional causal framework

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Vacuum-data uniqueness is an obstruction about complete data
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider an autonomous Einstein-matter theory that admits Minkowski spacetime with matter vacuum Ψ0 and has a unique smooth maximal globally hyperbolic Cauchy development, up to gauge and diffeomorphism. On a complete Cauchy surface Σ≅R³, specify h_ij=δ_ij, K_ij=0, Ψ=Ψ0 and all independent matter momenta equal to their vacuum values. Minkowski vacuum is one development of these data. Uniqueness therefore identifies every other development with it on its domain; a later curvature pulse is impossible there. This does not follow from h_ij and K_ij alone: nonvacuum source data can satisfy the gravitational constraints. Incoming preparation must already occur in complete initial data, or enter through a boundary if the surface was not actually a Cauchy surface.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Select a source that allows negative energy without a wrong-sign kinetic term
reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (−,+,+,+), natural units c=ℏ=1, κ=8πG, and S=∫d⁴x√−g[R/(2κ)−(1/2)g^{μν}∂_μφ∂_νφ−V(φ)], where V(φ)=(λ/a²)φ²(φ²−a²)(φ²−4a²), λ>0 and a>0. Both φ and a have energy units, λ is dimensionless, V has energy-density units, and κ has units energy⁻². The equations are G_μν=κT_μν and □φ−V'(φ)=0, with T_μν=∂_μφ∂_νφ−g_μν[(∂φ)²/2+V]. The potential is bounded below because its leading term is positive, but is negative for a<|φ|<2a. Thus negative normal energy is not ruled out for arbitrary data. The vacuum φ=0 has V=V'=0 and V''(0)=8λa²>0. This polynomial is a classical source model, not a demonstrated quantum-complete theory.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify the Cauchy problem and the distinction between constraints and full stress
reasoning_steps.argument: Let n be the unit future normal, π=n^μ∂_μφ, q_i=D_iφ, and ρ=T_μνn^μn^ν. Then ρ=(π²+q²)/2+V, j_i=−πq_i, and S_ij=q_iq_j+h_ij[(π²−q²)/2−V]. Complete data are (h,K,φ,π), subject to R^(3)+K²−K_ijK^ij=2κρ and D_j(K^{ij}−h^{ij}K)=κj^i, in a consistent extrinsic-curvature convention. Flat h and zero K require ρ=j=0, not S_ij=0. By contrast, an exactly Minkowski open prehistory requires the full T_μν=0 through Einstein's equations. For smooth data, the Einstein-scalar equations have the usual local hyperbolic Cauchy formulation in harmonic gauge; the potential changes lower-order terms, not the principal wave operator. The argument concerns the unique regular globally hyperbolic development and does not assume extension through a singularity.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Classify every stress-free scalar configuration on a slice
reasoning_steps.argument: For any unit spatial vector e, T(n,n)+T(e,e)=π²+(e·q)². If the entire tensor vanishes, this nonnegative sum is zero for every e. Therefore π=0 and q_i=0; substituting into ρ=0 gives V=0. Conversely these conditions make all components of T vanish. On connected Σ, φ must consequently be a spatial constant C with C∈{0,±a,±2a}. This classification does not assume V≥0 and leaves no smooth localized, stress-free scalar profile. Under the usual asymptotic matter condition φ→0, only C=0 remains. If that matter boundary condition is relaxed, the four other constants are genuine nonvacuum stress-free initial fields.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Nonvacuum stress-free fields evade the vacuum-data premise but not dynamics
reasoning_steps.argument: At the nonzero roots, V'(±a)=∓6λa³ and V'(±2a)=±48λa³, all nonzero. reasoning_steps.argument: Use signature (−,+,+,+), c=ℏ=1, κ=8πG, and S=∫√−g[R/(2κ)+P(X,φ)]d⁴x, with X=−g^{μν}∂_μφ∂_νφ/2. P is smooth with finite derivatives on the background. Taking φ to have energy units gives X and P units energy⁴, P_X dimensionless and P_XX units energy⁻⁴. The necessary local gate is a physical scalar mode with a nondegenerate Lorentzian principal symbol, a common spacelike initial surface with gravity, and positive high-frequency kinetic and gradient energies relative to the ordinary positive-energy gravitational sector. Passing this gate would not establish nonlinear stability or quantum consistency.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Re-establish the target's null-energy requirement
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the metric explicitly reproduced in the supplied cycle-2 extract: ds²=−dt²+(dx−b dt)²+dy²+dz², b=v(t)f. Define n=∂t+b∂x and e_x=∂x, an orthonormal timelike–spacelike pair. Writing b_i=∂_i b and Q=b_y²+b_z², direct curvature evaluation gives R(n,n)=−n(b_x)−b_x²−Q/2 and R(e_x,e_x)=n(b_x)+b_x²−Q/2. Thus R(n,n)+R(e_x,e_x)=−Q, including a time-dependent pulse; time derivatives cancel rather than being neglected. Einstein's equation implies T(n,n)+T(e_x,e_x)=−Q/κ. For k_±=n±e_x, T(k_+,k_+)+T(k_−,k_−)=−2Q/κ. At least one null contraction is strictly negative wherever the transverse wall gradient is nonzero. This conclusion does not follow merely from negative normal energy; the null contraction is an additional calculation.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Distinguish the geometry from local superluminal motion
reasoning_steps.argument: In that metric, a trajectory with dx=b dt and dy=dz=0 has ds²=−dt², and axial light rays obey dx/dt=b±1. Coordinate speeds exceeding one therefore need not mean motion outside the local metric light cone. Also g^{tt}=−1, so increasing t is a temporal orientation for this prescribed geometry. Neither observation supplies matter capable of producing it, establishes preparation or leading-wall control, or settles causality after combining configurations. The present calculation tests the source, not a working transport mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Derive null stress, equations and conservation
reasoning_steps.argument: Let u_μ=∂_μφ, A=P_X and B=P_XX. Variation gives T_μν=A u_μu_ν+P g_μν and E≡∇_μ(A∇^μφ)+P_φ=0. Consequently T_μνk^μk^ν=A(k·u)² for every metric-null k. Strict negative null stress requires A<0 and a nonzero contraction; the potential-like P term cannot change this sign. The identity ∇_μT^{μν}=E∇^νφ ensures stress conservation on solutions. Expanding E shows its second-derivative coefficient is Z^{μν}=A g^{μν}−B u^μu^ν; the remaining terms include P_φ−2X P_Xφ and are lower derivative.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Obtain the complete fixed-metric quadratic scalar action
reasoning_steps.argument: For φ=φ̄+π on a background solution, δX=−u·∇π−(∇π)²/2. The quadratic Lagrangian is L₂=−A(∇π)²/2+B(u·∇π)²/2−P_Xφ π u·∇π+P_φφ π²/2. Integrating the mixed term by parts yields L₂=−Z^{μν}∇_μπ∇_νπ/2+Uπ²/2, where U=P_φφ+∇_μ(P_Xφ u^μ). U has units energy². This is the fixed-background second variation; its frozen-coefficient principal part is the necessary short-wavelength test. Background variation and U affect long wavelengths but cannot reverse the leading derivative signs in a controlled high-frequency regime.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. A general-slicing Hamiltonian exposes the obstruction
reasoning_steps.argument: At a point choose a metric-orthonormal frame adapted to an arbitrary timelike normal and set q=∂tφ̄, s_i=∂iφ̄, so u^μ=(−q,s_i). Define K=A+Bq². Then L₂=Kπ̇²/2−Bqπ̇(s·∇π)−[A|∇π|²−B(s·∇π)²]/2+Uπ²/2. For K≠0, p=Kπ̇−Bq(s·∇π) and H₂=[p+Bq(s·∇π)]²/(2K)+[A|∇π|²−B(s·∇π)²]/2−Uπ²/2. If A<0 and K>0, take a wavevector perpendicular to s. The cross term vanishes and ω²=(A|k|²−U)/K, negative at sufficiently large |k|. Its growth rate approaches |k|√(−A/K). If K<0, the momentum-square term is negative: a ghost relative to ordinary matter and gravity. K=0 makes that slicing characteristic for the scalar. This argument holds for every metric-timelike normal and prevents a change of common slicing from restoring positive high-frequency energy.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Timelike-gradient classification
reasoning_steps.argument: For X>0 use the scalar rest frame u_μ=(√(2X),0,0,0) and define F=A+2XB. Then Z=diag(−F,A,A,A), L₂=Fπ̇²/2−A|∇π|²/2+Uπ²/2 and H₂=p²/(2F)+A|∇π|²/2−Uπ²/2. The frozen dispersion is ω²=(A/F)|k|²−U/F. Positive high-frequency energy requires F>0 and A>0, giving sound speed squared c_s²=A/F. If A<0,F>0 there is a gradient instability and the symbol is definite rather than Lorentzian. If A<0,F<0 the symbol is Lorentzian but the mode has negative kinetic energy. More generally, for nonzero A,F, timelike-gradient hyperbolicity requires AF>0; hyperbolicity alone does not select the healthy overall sign.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Spacelike-gradient classification
reasoning_steps.argument: For X<0 use u_μ=(0,√(−2X),0,0). Now Z=diag(−A,F,A,A), H₂=p²/(2A)+F(∂xπ)²/2+A[(∂yπ)²+(∂zπ)²]/2−Uπ²/2 and ω²=|k_⊥|²+(F/A)k_x²−U/A. Positive high-frequency energy again requires A>0,F>0. For A<0 the kinetic term is a ghost, regardless of B; varying B changes only the longitudinal spatial coefficient. With AF<0 the symbol has two eigenvalues of each sign and is not an ordinary Lorentzian wave operator. With A<0,F<0 it is Lorentzian but has the wrong energy sign. Thus choosing a spacelike background gradient does not evade the obstruction.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Null and zero-gradient backgrounds
reasoning_steps.argument: For a nonzero null gradient choose u_μ=(q,q,0,0), X=0. The principal-symbol determinant is det Z=−A⁴ in a metric-orthonormal frame, so A≠0 gives a Lorentzian symbol even for finite nonzero B. Nevertheless the general Hamiltonian test applies: if A<0, K=A+Bq² is either negative, zero, or positive with unstable transverse modes. A Lorentzian symbol therefore does not rescue negative null stress. For A>0 a boost can make |q| small enough that both kinetic and spatial-gradient coefficients are positive locally; its null stress is then nonnegative. If u=0, Z=A g and all null stresses vanish; A<0 is an ordinary wrong-sign scalar, while A=0 has no quadratic derivative term.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Degenerate boundaries for non-null gradients
reasoning_steps.argument: The determinant identity is det Z=−A³F. For X>0, A=0,F≠0 leaves only a time-derivative quadratic term: F>0 is not itself a ghost, but there is no spatial restoring term and no nondegenerate wave cone. F=0,A≠0 removes the rest-frame time kinetic term, leaving a spatial constraint rather than a scalar wave equation. For X<0, A=0,F≠0 leaves only a longitudinal spatial derivative and no time kinetic term; F=0,A≠0 leaves a rank-three operator describing transverse propagation without a longitudinal principal derivative. If A=F=0 at nonzero X, then B=0 and the derivative quadratic form vanishes entirely. These are rank deficiencies, not automatically proofs of inconsistency of every possible constrained formulation. A=0, however, gives zero—not strictly negative—null stress; F=0 with A<0 does not provide a regular positive-energy scalar wave.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Null degeneracy, constrained exceptions and crossing boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: For nonzero null u and A=0, Z=−B u^μu^ν has rank one when B≠0 and rank zero when B=0. It is not a nondegenerate hyperbolic scalar operator and its null stress vanishes. A concrete different boundary is P=−μ²√(2X)−V(φ) on X>0: A=−μ²/√(2X)<0 but F=0. It can violate the null energy condition, yet its scalar equation has a spatial-constraint principal part in the gradient rest frame, not a propagating hyperbolic scalar. Whether a coupled constrained model of this kind is predictive and stable needs a separate elliptic–hyperbolic analysis; it is not ruled out as incoherent here. Higher-derivative terms can also change degenerate dispersion, but change the specified action. Smooth passage through A=0 cannot avoid the obstruction inside any open region where strict negative null stress requires A<0.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Why ordinary gravitational coupling does not remove the local bad mode
reasoning_steps.argument: In a regular minimally coupled Einstein–P system, the linearized Einstein equations contain second derivatives of the metric, but δT contains at most first derivatives of π. The scalar equation contains second derivatives of π with coefficient Z and at most first derivatives of metric perturbations through connection variations and coefficient derivatives. Thus the leading second-order principal blocks in harmonic gauge are the Einstein wave block and Z. In a short-wavelength regime above background, mass and mixing scales, gravitational constraints do not reverse the scalar principal energy sign; choosing unitary gauge merely relocates the physical scalar perturbation into the metric variables. For an exact classical P theory arbitrarily large wave numbers are available. For an effective theory the inference requires a window between those scales and its cutoff. If no such window exists, the proposed description is uncontrolled, not evidence that an unknown ultraviolet completion is impossible.

reasoning_steps.title: Fix the metric, curvature convention and measured components
reasoning_steps.argument: Take signature (−,+,+,+), x⁰=ct, zero cosmological constant, and G_ab=8πG T_ab/c⁴. Use R(X,Y)Z=∇_X∇_Y Z−∇_Y∇_X Z−∇_[X,Y]Z and its usual Ricci contraction. The metric is ds²=−(dx⁰)²+[dx−u dx⁰]²+dy²+dz², where u=βf(r), r²=(x−βx⁰)²+y²+z² and β is constant. The profile is smooth, equals one for r≤R and zero for r≥R+Δ, with R,Δ>0. An orthonormal frame is n=∂₀+u∂ₓ and e_i=∂_i. Define ε=T(n,n), j_i=−T(n,e_i), S_ij=T(e_i,e_j), and C=c⁴/(8πG). Thus the covariant frame matrix has first row (ε,−j_x,−j_y,−j_z). This sign is essential for the null contractions.

reasoning_steps.title: Define derivatives and compute the constraints
reasoning_steps.argument: Write a=u_x, b=u_y, d=u_z, Q=b²+d², and L=u_yy+u_zz. Let D act on scalars as n: because ∂₀u=−βu_x and likewise for its spatial derivatives, D=(u−β)∂ₓ on these translating quantities. With K_ij=−(1/2)L_n h_ij, lapse one, h_ij=δ_ij and shift B=−u e_x, K has rows (−a,−b/2,−d/2), (−b/2,0,0), (−d/2,0,0). Hence K=−a and K_ijK^ij=a²+Q/2. The Hamiltonian constraint gives ε/C=(K²−K_ijK^ij)/2=−Q/4. The momentum constraint gives j_i/C=∂_jK^j_i−∂_iK, so j_x/C=−L/2, j_y/C=u_xy/2 and j_z/C=u_xz/2.

reasoning_steps.title: Extract the spatial stresses from the evolution equation
reasoning_steps.argument: For the stated K convention, the unit-lapse evolution equation is (∂₀−L_B)K_ij=K K_ij−2K_ikK^k_j−[S_ij−δ_ij(S−ε)/2]/C, since the intrinsic spatial Ricci tensor vanishes. Define M_ij=(∂₀−L_B)K_ij and P_ij=K K_ij−2K_ikK^k_j−M_ij. Explicitly, M_xx=−Da−2a², M_xy=−Db/2−3ab/2, M_xz=−Dd/2−3ad/2, M_yy=−b², M_zz=−d² and M_yz=−bd. Subtraction gives P_xx=Da+a²−Q/2, P_xy=Db/2+ab, P_xz=Dd/2+ad, P_yy=b²/2, P_zz=d²/2 and P_yz=bd/2. Its trace is P=Da+a². Taking the trace of the evolution equation gives S/C=3ε/C−2P; substituting back gives S_ij/C=P_ij+δ_ij(ε/C−P). This determines all six independent stresses without a matter equation-of-state assumption.

reasoning_steps.title: State the complete orthonormal source
reasoning_steps.argument: Define A=Da+a²=β²[(f−1)f_xx+f_x²], B_y=Db/2+ab=β²[(f−1)f_xy/2+f_xf_y], and B_z=Dd/2+ad=β²[(f−1)f_xz/2+f_xf_z]. The ten independent components are: ε=−CQ/4; (j_x,j_y,j_z)=(C/2)(−L,u_xy,u_xz); S_xx=−3CQ/4; S_xy=CB_y; S_xz=CB_z; S_yy=C[(b²−d²)/4−A]; S_zz=C[(d²−b²)/4−A]; and S_yz=Cbd/2. Here Q=β²(f_y²+f_z²), L=β(f_yy+f_zz), b=βf_y and d=βf_z. Symmetry supplies the remaining entries. These are energy density, momentum-density projections and stresses in the specified normal frame, all with units J/m³; they are not a demonstrated material constitutive law.

reasoning_steps.title: Check the axial null contractions by a separate frame-curvature route
reasoning_steps.argument: The frame commutators are [n,e_i]=−u_i e_x and [e_i,e_j]=0. Put H_ij=(δ_ix u_j+δ_jx u_i)/2 and Ω_ij=(δ_ix u_j−δ_jx u_i)/2. The Koszul formula gives ∇_n n=0, ∇_i n=H_ij e_j, ∇_i e_j=H_ij n and ∇_n e_i=Ω_ij e_j. Direct curvature contraction then gives R_nn=−Da−a²−Q/2. reasoning_steps.argument: The two null contractions sum to −2CQ. At any point with β≠0 and f_y²+f_z²>0, their sum is strictly negative, so at least one is negative. reasoning_steps.argument: Every component vanishes for β=0 or a constant profile, as required for the corresponding flat metric. The ten independent components are: ε=−CQ/4; (j_x,j_y,j_z)=(C/2)(−L,u_xy,u_xz); S_xx=−3CQ/4; S_xy=CB_y; S_xz=CB_z; S_yy=C[(b²−d²)/4−A]; S_zz=C[(d²−b²)/4−A]; and S_yz=Cbd/2. Here Q=β²(f_y²+f_z²), L=β(f_yy+f_zz), b=βf_y and d=βf_z. Symmetry supplies the remaining entries. These are energy density, momentum-density projections and stresses in the specified normal frame, all with units J/m³; they are not a demonstrated material constitutive law.

review.rationale: Substituting ε/C=−Q/4 and P=Da+a² into the preceding inversion reproduces every listed stress. Expanding u=βf gives the displayed A and B terms, and C times inverse-length-squared has units J/m³.

argument_steps.title: Check the axial null contractions by a separate frame-curvature route
argument_steps.argument: The frame commutators are [n,e_i]=−u_i e_x and [e_i,e_j]=0. Put H_ij=(δ_ix u_j+δ_jx u_i)/2 and Ω_ij=(δ_ix u_j−δ_jx u_i)/2. The Koszul formula gives ∇_n n=0, ∇_i n=H_ij e_j, ∇_i e_j=H_ij n and ∇_n e_i=Ω_ij e_j. Direct curvature contraction then gives R_nn=−Da−a²−Q/2. For R_xx, the normal contribution is Da+a²−Q/4, while the two spatial contributions sum to −Q/4, giving R_xx=Da+a²−Q/2. For R_nx, the spatial contraction leaves (∂_y b+∂_z d)/2=L/2. Therefore R_nn+R_xx=−Q. Since k_±=n±e_x are null, the scalar-curvature term in Einstein's equation drops out: T(k_±,k_±)=C(R_nn+R_xx±2R_nx)=C(−Q±L). This is exactly the questioned formula. The full-source check gives the same result directly from ε+S_xx∓2j_x. These are two hand-calculation routes, not external verification.

review.rationale: The commutators and Koszul connection have the stated signs. Their Ricci projections give R_nn+R_xx=−Q and R_nx=L/2. Null contraction removes the scalar-curvature term and agrees with ε+S_xx∓2j_x.

argument_steps.title: Identify precisely the pointwise NEC failure and edge cases
argument_steps.argument: The two null contractions sum to −2CQ. At any point with β≠0 and f_y²+f_z²>0, their sum is strictly negative, so at least one is negative. More explicitly their minimum is C[−β²(f_y²+f_z²)−|β(f_yy+f_zz)|]. A nontrivial smooth spherical wall has an open region with f′≠0 and nonzero transverse radius, hence Q>0 there. This proves pointwise NEC failure without requiring |β|>1 or a monotone profile. If Q=0 but L≠0, one of these directions still violates NEC. If Q=L=0, these two tests vanish and do not decide all other null directions. For any unit spatial vector s, the complete local test is T(n+s,n+s)=ε−2j_i s_i+S_ij s_i s_j.

review.rationale: The sum is strictly negative when Q>0, so at least one direction violates NEC. A smooth spherical profile changing between its prescribed endpoints has an open region with f′≠0 and nonzero transverse radius. The Q=L=0 caveat correctly leaves other null directions undecided.

argument_steps.title: Perform consistency and limiting checks
argument_steps.argument: Every component vanishes for β=0 or a constant profile, as required for the corresponding flat metric. The trace predicts scalar curvature R=(ε−S)/C=2A+Q/2; together with the independently calculated R_nn, this gives G_nn=R_nn+R/2=−Q/4, recovering the Hamiltonian constraint. In the auxiliary one-dimensional reduction f=f(x−βx⁰), Q=L=0 and all fluxes vanish: ε=S_xx=0, S_yy=S_zz=−CA, with other stresses zero. This agrees with a curved two-dimensional (x⁰,x) factor times a flat transverse plane: the Einstein tensor vanishes within the two-dimensional factor and equals −R/2 in each transverse direction. Finally, C has units J/m and all quantities multiplying it have units m⁻².

review.rationale: The flat limits remove all derivatives. Tracing the stresses gives R=2A+Q/2 and hence G_nn=−Q/4. In the one-dimensional product reduction, the two-dimensional Einstein tensor vanishes and the transverse components equal −R/2, matching the source.

argument_steps.title: Separate pointwise null vectors from affine ANEC geodesics
argument_steps.argument: ANEC concerns I_γ=∫T_ab ℓ^aℓ^b dλ on a specified complete affinely parametrized null geodesic, with convergence and completeness checked. Write ℓ=ω(n+s_i e_i), |s|=1 and ω=dx⁰/dλ>0. The frame connection above gives dω/dλ=−ω² s_x(∇u·s), ds_i/dλ=ω s_x[(∇u·s)s_i−u_i], dx/dλ=ω(u+s_x), dy/dλ=ωs_y and dz/dλ=ωs_z. The integrand is ω²[ε−2j·s+S_ij s_i s_j]. These equations preserve |s|=1. In general, initially choosing s=±e_x does not keep it axial: ds_y/dλ=∓ωu_y and ds_z/dλ=∓ωu_z at that instant. Even on the symmetry axis, where those transverse derivatives vanish, dω/dλ=−ω²u_x need not vanish. Thus the local pair k_± is not a pair of globally affine null tangents, and its negative sum cannot be integrated as an ANEC proof. No complete affine integral has been evaluated here.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify the spacetime, profile and normalization
reasoning_steps.argument: Let t=x⁰=ct_phys, ξ=x−βt, r²=ξ²+y²+z² and M=R⁴ with signature (−,+,+,+). Take ds²=−dt²+[dx−βf(r)dt]²+dy²+dz², β>1, and C=c⁴/(8πG), with G_ab=T_ab/C and zero cosmological constant. Define η(s)=exp(−1/s) for s>0 and η(s)=0 otherwise. For R,Δ>0 put s=(r−R)/Δ and f(r)=η(1−s)/[η(s)+η(1−s)]. This is C∞, equals one for r≤R, vanishes for r≥R+Δ and is strictly decreasing in the wall. The constant core ensures smoothness at r=0. Take affine λ to have units of length, so ω=dt/dλ is dimensionless. Future direction means ω>0.

reasoning_steps.title: Locate and characterize both axial zeros
reasoning_steps.argument: On the axis define a(ξ)=1−β+βf(|ξ|). There is exactly one h∈(R,R+Δ) satisfying f(h)=1−1/β. Hence a vanishes precisely at ξ=−h and ξ=+h, is positive between them, and is negative outside. In the wall, f′(r)=−f(1−f)[s⁻²+(1−s)⁻²]/Δ<0. Set κ=−βf′(h)>0, with units m⁻¹. Then a′(−h)=+κ and a′(+h)=−κ, so both zeros are simple. These are axial characteristic separatrices; no claim that the full spherical surface r=h is a global event horizon is needed.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the affine first integrals
reasoning_steps.argument: Write w=β(1−f)=1−a. In comoving coordinates the metric is ds²=−dt²+(dξ+w dt)²+dy²+dz². On the axis the forward null tangent is ℓ=ω(∂t+a∂ξ), corresponding to n+e_x in the normal frame. Reflection symmetry preserves axial motion. The stationary Killing field K=∂t gives E=−g(K,ℓ)=ωa. The affine frequency equation is ω′=−ω²a′(ξ), where the prime on ω denotes d/dλ and on a denotes d/dξ. Thus d(ωa)/dλ=0 and dξ/dλ=E. Equivalently, away from a zero, ξ=Eλ+constant and dt/dξ=1/a. These equations also follow from the axial metric's conserved momentum and null constraint. E has the same sign as a because ω>0.

reasoning_steps.title: Classify all nonzero-E forward rays
reasoning_steps.argument: There are three sectors. For ξ<−h, E<0: toward the future ξ decreases to −∞ at infinite affine parameter; toward the past ξ approaches −h at finite affine parameter. For −h<ξ<h, E>0: ξ increases from −h to +h, with both endpoints at finite affine parameter and total affine interval 2h/E. For ξ>h, E<0: the past runs to +∞ at infinite affine parameter and the future approaches +h at finite affine parameter. Near either zero ξ_h, let q=a′(ξ_h)=±κ. Then t=q⁻¹ ln(|ξ−ξ_h|/Δ)+O(1). Consequently every approach to −h occurs at t→−∞ and every approach to +h occurs at t→+∞. These are maximal rays in M: the finite-affine limit has no finite-t point in M. In the exterior, a=1−β is constant, so the stated infinite ends really are affine-complete ends, not just coordinate-distance limits.

reasoning_steps.title: Include the missing E=0 generators
reasoning_steps.argument: A nonzero future null tangent with E=0 must have a=0. Its trajectory is ξ=ξ_h, y=z=0 for all real t. Along it, dω/dλ=−qω², so ω=1/[q(λ−λ_c)] and λ−λ_c=exp[q(t−t₀)]/(qω₀), where ω₀>0. At ξ=−h, q=κ and λ ranges over (λ_c,∞): the generator is past incomplete and future complete. At ξ=+h, q=−κ and λ ranges over (−∞,λ_c): it is past complete and future incomplete. Thus an orbit extending through every real coordinate time need not be affinely complete. These generators together with the three nonzero-E sectors exhaust the forward axial family.

reasoning_steps.title: Compute transverse tidal curvature directly
reasoning_steps.argument: At y=z=0, first transverse derivatives of w vanish and w_yy=w_zz=−βf′(r)/r. For longitudinal indices A,B∈{t,ξ}, g_AB has entries g_tt=w²−1, g_tξ=w and g_ξξ=1. Because g_yy=g_zz=1 and the first transverse metric derivatives vanish on the axis, R_AyBy=−(1/2)∂²_y g_AB there. Contracting with ℓ^A=ω(1,a), and using w+a=1, yields R(ℓ,e_y,ℓ,e_y)=βf′(r)ω²/r; the z contraction is identical. The coordinate unit vectors e_y and e_z are parallelly transported along an axial ray, since Γ^μ_Ay=Γ^μ_Az=0 there. The null Ricci contraction is the sum over these two screen directions, giving R_abℓ^aℓ^b=2βf′(r)ω²/r and T_abℓ^aℓ^b=2Cβf′(r)ω²/r. If a regular C² extension continued the affine geodesic through such an endpoint, its tangent and parallel screen frame would be finite there and its continuous curvature would have finite contractions, contradicting this divergence. reasoning_steps.argument: On the axis define a(ξ)=1−β+βf(|ξ|). There is exactly one h∈(R,R+Δ) satisfying f(h)=1−1/β. argument_steps.title: Specify the spacetime, profile and normalization
argument_steps.argument: Let t=x⁰=ct_phys, ξ=x−βt, r²=ξ²+y²+z² and M=R⁴ with signature (−,+,+,+). Take ds²=−dt²+[dx−βf(r)dt]²+dy²+dz², β>1, and C=c⁴/(8πG), with G_ab=T_ab/C and zero cosmological constant. Define η(s)=exp(−1/s) for s>0 and η(s)=0 otherwise. For R,Δ>0 put s=(r−R)/Δ and f(r)=η(1−s)/[η(s)+η(1−s)]. This is C∞, equals one for r≤R, vanishes for r≥R+Δ and is strictly decreasing in the wall. The constant core ensures smoothness at r=0. Take affine λ to have units of length, so ω=dt/dλ is dimensionless. Future direction means ω>0.

review.rationale: Accepted as explicit conditional premises, not physical existence evidence. The denominator defining f never vanishes; the smooth flat endpoints give a compact wall, and the constant core removes the radial-coordinate smoothness issue at the origin. The affine and time units are consistent.

argument_steps.title: Locate and characterize both axial zeros
argument_steps.argument: On the axis define a(ξ)=1−β+βf(|ξ|). There is exactly one h∈(R,R+Δ) satisfying f(h)=1−1/β. Hence a vanishes precisely at ξ=−h and ξ=+h, is positive between them, and is negative outside. In the wall, f′(r)=−f(1−f)[s⁻²+(1−s)⁻²]/Δ<0. Set κ=−βf′(h)>0, with units m⁻¹. Then a′(−h)=+κ and a′(+h)=−κ, so both zeros are simple. These are axial characteristic separatrices; no claim that the full spherical surface r=h is a global event horizon is needed.

review.rationale: The wall derivative is strictly negative, so each intermediate value occurs exactly once. Differentiating f(|ξ|) gives opposite signs at ±h, yielding precisely the two stated simple zeros and κ>0.

argument_steps.title: Derive the affine first integrals
argument_steps.argument: Write w=β(1−f)=1−a. In comoving coordinates the metric is ds²=−dt²+(dξ+w dt)²+dy²+dz². On the axis the forward null tangent is ℓ=ω(∂t+a∂ξ), corresponding to n+e_x in the normal frame. Reflection symmetry preserves axial motion. The stationary Killing field K=∂t gives E=−g(K,ℓ)=ωa. The affine frequency equation is ω′=−ω²a′(ξ), where the prime on ω denotes d/dλ and on a denotes d/dξ. Thus d(ωa)/dλ=0 and dξ/dλ=E. Equivalently, away from a zero, ξ=Eλ+constant and dt/dξ=1/a. These equations also follow from the axial metric's conserved momentum and null constraint. E has the same sign as a because ω>0.

review.rationale: For the stationary axial metric, direct contraction with ∂t gives E=ωa. Combining the frequency equation with ξ′=ωa makes E constant and therefore ξ affine-linear. Reflection symmetry makes the axial restriction consistent.

argument_steps.title: Classify all nonzero-E forward rays
argument_steps.argument: There are three sectors. For ξ<−h, E<0: toward the future ξ decreases to −∞ at infinite affine parameter; toward the past ξ approaches −h at finite affine parameter. For −h<ξ<h, E>0: ξ increases from −h to +h, with both endpoints at finite affine parameter and total affine interval 2h/E. For ξ>h, E<0: the past runs to +∞ at infinite affine parameter and the future approaches +h at finite affine parameter. Near either zero ξ_h, let q=a′(ξ_h)=±κ. Then t=q⁻¹ ln(|ξ−ξ_h|/Δ)+O(1). Consequently every approach to −h occurs at t→−∞ and every approach to +h occurs at t→+∞. These are maximal rays in M: the finite-affine limit has no finite-t point in M. In the exterior, a=1−β is constant, so the stated infinite ends really are affine-complete ends, not just coordinate-distance limits.

review.rationale: The signs of E and a determine each sector's orientation. Since ξ′ is a nonzero constant, a finite ξ boundary is reached in finite affine parameter, whereas spatial infinity requires infinite parameter. Integrating dt/dξ=1/a gives the stated logarithmic time limits, so no endpoint lies in M.

argument_steps.title: Include the missing E=0 generators
argument_steps.argument: A nonzero future null tangent with E=0 must have a=0. Its trajectory is ξ=ξ_h, y=z=0 for all real t. Along it, dω/dλ=−qω², so ω=1/[q(λ−λ_c)] and λ−λ_c=exp[q(t−t₀)]/(qω₀), where ω₀>0. At ξ=−h, q=κ and λ ranges over (λ_c,∞): the generator is past incomplete and future complete. At ξ=+h, q=−κ and λ ranges over (−∞,λ_c): it is past complete and future incomplete. Thus an orbit extending through every real coordinate time need not be affinely complete. These generators together with the three nonzero-E sectors exhaust the forward axial family.
